problem: Provide a pretrained manipulation policy that can be adapted to new observation modalities, action spaces and robots without discarding its pretrained backbone.
contribution: Octo uses modular task/observation tokenizers, block-wise transformer attention and a continuous diffusion action head, pretrained on a curated800Ktrajectory mixture.
algorithm: Encode language/goal images and temporal observations into modality tokens. Mask absent modalities; observation tokens attend causally, while readout tokens passively summarize prior inputs. Decode action chunks with a small DDPM head after one backbone pass. Add new tokenizers/heads and finetune the full model for target contracts.
observations: Language or goal images, third-person/wrist histories and optionally new proprioceptive modalities. Missing input tokens are masked rather than treated as measured zeros.
actions: Continuous multimodal action chunks; finetuning supports joint-position heads and new robots. Pretraining aligns gripper+1open/0closed and zero-pads missing camera channels.
embodiment_and_data: 800Kcurated Open-X trajectories from an approximately1.5Mepisode pool. Real evaluations cover9setups across4institutions, including joint control, bimanual tasks and force-torque input adaptation.
experiments: Finetuning recipe uses around100target demonstrations and50Ksteps. TableI evaluates20trials/domain; direct policies use2language tasks/robot with10trials each. Source evaluates new inputs/actions separately from in-distribution zero-shot setups.
baselines: RT-1-X/RT-2-X zero-shot, target-only ResNet+Transformer and pretrained VC-1 representations for finetuning; MSE/discrete-action heads and data-mixture/model-scale ablations. RT-X has a smaller350Kpretraining subset, so not a pure architecture-only comparison.

quantitative_result.value: TableI average finetuning success72% forOcto versus20%fromscratch and15%VC-1; each domain20trials and approximately100demonstrations. This aggregate does not imply72% on an unseen Explorer robot.

limitations: Wrist-camera finetuning can be worse than third-person only; only27%ofpretraining data has wrist inputs and56%language annotations. Trains from optimal demonstrations, not a demonstrated online-improvement method; mobile manipulation is future scope.
code_and_license: Paper reports public training/finetuning tools; this review did not inspect source files or verify separate code/model/data rights. No Octo execution is claimed.
hardware_adaptation: A relevant compact-policy reference, but adapting robot inputs/actions requires real processors, finetuning and evaluation. Overview-only sensing does not inherit force-torque experiments. Record modality presence and gripper semantics explicitly.
